newsitem.title: USA: Illinois governor signs $659 mln GO bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Illinois governor signs $659 mln GO bond bill.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar signed into law Thursday a bill authorizing the issuance of $659 million of general obligation bonds for capital projects.
The bill signing came just a day after the bill was passed by the Democrat-controlled House, after passing the Senate earlier this month.
House action on the bill followed an agreement struck between the Republican governor and legislative leaders a week ago.

House Democrats, who opposed the bill over the last two legislative session, signed onto it after Edgar was able to convince House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, that many of the projects, including prisons, were needed on an emergency basis and that the state's financial position had improved as underscored by Moody's Investors Service's upgrade of the state's GO rating Feb. 10.
